Are we reaching the limits of current AI infrastructure, or are platform bugs just getting worse?

As a developer, I monitor how these systems perform daily. This week, we are seeing significant technical friction across major LLM providers, from unexpected rate limits to critical billing and UI glitches.

Here is what is happening on the ground right now.

💸 A frustrating iOS billing bug in OpenAI's system is double-charging users. One developer trying to purchase 100 ChatGPT credits for 4 dollars was charged 15 times after receiving repeated errors, leaving them with zero credits and no human support.

📉 Anthropic users are reporting sudden, unexplained changes to their weekly usage limits. One developer on the paid 20x plan found their account at 61 percent usage on Friday afternoon despite only running two sessions.

🖥️ The OpenAI 5.6 Sol interface is experiencing severe freezing issues. Users attempting to generate lists of obscure items in Work mode report that the web and mobile apps lock up completely as soon as the chat history is opened.

💼 On the commercial side, new monetization strategies are focusing on practical ways to earn 5,000 rupees daily using Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini, highlighting what clients actually pay for prompt engineering and automations.

These issues highlight a growing gap between rapid feature releases and stable infrastructure. When basic billing and usage tracking fail, it impacts production workflows.

Have you noticed any sudden drops in your Claude usage limits or encountered interface freezes this week?
